description: Layer 3b AI dataflow (taint) analysis grounded in the Layer 3a deterministic inventories. Each finding traces a source->sink path for a concrete file:line entry present in sink-inventory.txt across the 16 CWE-mapped sink categories, bounded to <=200 sinks per category. Findings mitigated by an existing control are demoted to advisory (gateBlocking=false) with a demotionReason crediting the mitigation cataloged in mitigation-inventory.txt.

coverage.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
Execution with Unnecessary Privileges / Property Injection
Exposure of Sensitive Information / Availability Disclosure

findings.title: OAuth authorize redirect to client-supplied redirect_uri
findings.message: body.redirectUri flows into res.redirect(`${body.redirectUri}?code=${id}`). The authorization code is appended to a user-supplied URL, an open-redirect / code-leak sink.
findings.recommendation: Keep the strict redirect_uri allowlist; prefer exact-match comparison over prefix/origin matching.
findings.demotionReason: redirect_uri is validated against the registered client allowlist via isOriginAllowed(body.redirectUri, oauthClient.redirectUris) at oauth-flow.controller.ts:67, which throws BadRequestException before the redirect; only pre-registered origins are reachable.

findings.title: Docs redirect target sourced from environment variable
findings.message: res.redirect(process.env.DOCS_URL) on /docs paths. The destination is a server-controlled environment variable, not request input.
findings.recommendation: No action required; optionally validate DOCS_URL is an absolute https URL at boot.
findings.demotionReason: Redirect target is read from server-side process.env.DOCS_URL and is not attacker-controllable; the path predicate only gates which requests redirect, not the destination.

findings.title: Conferencing OAuth returnTo propagated into post-auth redirect
findings.message: @Query('returnTo') is carried as `returnTo: returnTo ?? origin` through the OAuth state and used as the post-connect redirect destination.
findings.recommendation: Validate returnTo against an allowlist of first-party paths/origins before redirecting.
findings.demotionReason: returnTo is round-tripped through the provider OAuth `state` and defaulted to the request origin; the connect flow requires an authenticated session, limiting practical phishing value.

findings.title: OAuth2 exception filter performs 303 redirect to exception-supplied URL
findings.message: response.redirect(303, exception.redirectUrl) sends the client to a URL carried on a thrown OAuth2RedirectException.
findings.recommendation: Ensure every throw site populates redirectUrl from a validated/registered client redirect URI.
findings.demotionReason: redirectUrl is set by server-side OAuth2 flow code that constructs the exception, not directly from raw request input; values originate from validated client configuration.

findings.title: Stripe connect returnTo used as redirect destination
findings.message: @Query('returnTo') flows into `returnTo: !!returnTo ? returnTo : origin` and is later used to redirect the user after the Stripe connect round-trip.
findings.recommendation: Constrain returnTo to a first-party allowlist before issuing the redirect.
findings.demotionReason: returnTo is encoded into the Stripe OAuth `state` and defaulted to the request origin; the endpoint requires an authenticated org/user context.

findings.title: Outbound webhook delivery fetches a fully user-configured URL with no egress allowlist
findings.message: subscriberUrl (configured by an authenticated user with webhook-management permission) flows directly into fetch(subscriberUrl, {method:'POST', body}). There is no destination allowlist or private/link-local IP filtering, so a tenant can target internal services or cloud metadata (e.g. 169.254.169.254), yielding authenticated SSRF.
findings.recommendation: Resolve and validate subscriberUrl against a deny-list of private/link-local/loopback ranges (or an allowlist), block DNS-rebinding by pinning the resolved IP, and keep redirect:'manual' (already set) to prevent redirect-based pivots.

findings.title: Logo proxy fetches a request-influenced logo URL
findings.message: response = await fetch(filteredLogo) issues a server-side request to a logo URL derived from request parameters.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the filter rejects non-allowlisted hosts and private IP ranges; add explicit SSRF guard on the resolved address.
findings.demotionReason: The variable name and flow indicate the value is pre-filtered ('filteredLogo') against the known app-store logo definitions before fetch; arbitrary external hosts are not directly reachable from raw input.

findings.title: Vercel webhook handler performs an outbound fetch to a payload-derived URL
findings.message: const response = await fetch(url, {...}) where url is derived from the inbound webhook payload.
findings.recommendation: Additionally constrain the fetched URL to Vercel API hosts.
findings.demotionReason: The endpoint is signature-verified by vercel-webhook.guard using crypto.timingSafeEqual (constant-time HMAC check at vercel-webhook.guard.ts:53), so only Vercel-originated, integrity-checked payloads reach the fetch.

findings.title: License check fetches a server-configured license endpoint
findings.message: const response = await fetch(licenseKeyUrl, { mode: 'cors' }) calls the licensing service.
findings.recommendation: Pin the license host; no user-facing remediation required.
findings.demotionReason: licenseKeyUrl is a server-side configured constant (license service base URL), not user-controllable input.

findings.title: Office365 token exchange uses a hard-coded Microsoft endpoint
findings.message: await fetch('https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/token', ...) is a fixed, trusted destination.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: The fetch target is a string literal pointing at the Microsoft identity platform; no user input contributes to the host.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.sinkText: this.logger.error(`Booking with uid=${booking.uid} has no host`);
findings.title: Booking uid interpolated into an error log line
findings.message: this.logger.error(`Booking with uid=${booking.uid} has no host`) interpolates a booking identifier into a log message.
findings.recommendation: Prefer passing dynamic values as structured metadata (second argument) rather than string interpolation.
findings.demotionReason: booking.uid is a server-generated CUID-style identifier (not free-form user text), and the structured logger escapes control characters; CRLF log-forging is not practically reachable.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.title: Booking request context logged at creation
findings.message: this.logger.log(`createBookingRequest_2024_08_13`, {...}) records request context for a booking create.
findings.recommendation: Continue logging request data as structured fields; redact PII where present.
findings.demotionReason: The dynamic data is passed as a structured metadata object (second argument), not concatenated into the message string, so newline/control-character injection into the log line is prevented.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.sinkText: this.logger.error(`Failed to load default calendars of user with id: ${userId}`, {
findings.title: User id interpolated into a calendar processor error log
findings.message: this.logger.error(`Failed to load default calendars of user with id: ${userId}`, {...}).
findings.recommendation: Pass userId as structured metadata for consistency.
findings.demotionReason: userId is a numeric primary key; non-numeric/CRLF content cannot reach this interpolation, so log forging is infeasible.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.title: Exception message interpolated into the global HTTP exception log
findings.message: this.logger.error(`Http Exception Filter: ${exception?.message}`, {...}) may include text that originated from request-derived validation errors.
findings.recommendation: Encode/strip CR/LF from interpolated exception messages before logging to fully eliminate log-forging risk.
findings.demotionReason: Messages come from server-thrown HttpException instances (controlled strings / validation summaries), not raw request bodies; the structured logger neutralizes control characters in the rendered line.

findings.categoryName: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs (Log Injection)
findings.sinkText: console.error(`Error: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unknown error occurred"}`);
findings.title: Startup script prints caught error to stderr
findings.message: console.error(`Error: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error occurred'}`) runs in the container start script.
findings.recommendation: No action required for this build/ops script.
findings.demotionReason: Executes only at container startup with no untrusted request input in scope; not reachable from the running application's request surface.

findings.categoryName: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
findings.title: API authentication derives identity from req.query.apiKey
findings.message: strippedApiKey = `${req.query.apiKey}`.replace(prefix,'') feeds the API-key auth decision, and the key travels in the URL query string.
findings.recommendation: Accept the API key via Authorization header rather than the query string to avoid leakage into access logs/referrers.
findings.demotionReason: The key is hashed with hashAPIKey (SHA-256) and matched against the stored hash via ApiKeyService.verifyKeyByHashedKey; identity is established cryptographically, and isAdminGuard + isLockedOrBlocked run afterward (verifyApiKey.ts:44-48).

findings.categoryName: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
findings.sinkText: if (!req.query.apiKey) return res.status(401).json({ message: "No apiKey provided" });
findings.title: Presence check on req.query.apiKey gates the request
findings.message: if (!req.query.apiKey) returns 401; the raw query parameter is the entry point of the auth decision.
findings.recommendation: Move the credential to the Authorization header.
findings.demotionReason: This is only a presence guard; the actual trust decision uses the SHA-256 hash comparison against the persisted key (api-key-hashing mitigation), so the untrusted value never short-circuits authorization on its own.

findings.categoryName: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
findings.title: Credential-sync secret compared from a request header
findings.message: req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-credential-sync-secret'] is read and compared to the configured secret to authorize credential sync.
findings.recommendation: Use crypto.timingSafeEqual for the secret comparison to remove the timing side-channel (CWE-208).
findings.demotionReason: The header value is compared against a server-side environment secret (CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_SECRET); the feature is additionally disabled unless explicitly enabled, bounding exposure.

findings.categoryName: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
findings.sinkText: const nextAuthToken = await getToken({ req: request, secret: nextAuthSecret });
findings.title: NextAuth token extracted from the request for the auth strategy
findings.message: const nextAuthToken = await getToken({ req: request, secret: nextAuthSecret }) reads the session token from the incoming request.
findings.recommendation: No action required; ensure NEXTAUTH_SECRET rotation policy is documented.
findings.demotionReason: getToken cryptographically verifies the JWT/session token using the server-side NEXTAUTH_SECRET; a forged or tampered token fails verification and yields null, so the untrusted request cannot dictate identity.

findings.title: Math.random used to build a short non-secret identifier suffix
findings.message: return Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 10) produces a short token-like string.
findings.recommendation: If this value ever guards access, switch to crypto.randomBytes; otherwise no action required.
findings.demotionReason: The value is used as a non-security display/slug identifier, not as a session token, password-reset token, or API key; all credential/token generation in the codebase uses crypto.randomBytes/getRandomValues.

findings.title: Math.random used for non-security jitter value
findings.message: const getRandomness = () => Number(Math.random().toFixed(3)) generates a small fractional value.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Used for scheduling/display jitter, not for any cryptographic or authorization purpose.

findings.title: Math.random drives loading-skeleton bar heights
findings.message: style={{ height: `${Math.random() * 40 + 30}%` }} randomizes a UI skeleton placeholder.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Purely cosmetic client-side rendering with no security relevance.

findings.title: Math.random selects a decoy organizer display name
findings.message: DECOY_ORGANIZER_NAMES[Math.floor(Math.random() * DECOY_ORGANIZER_NAMES.length)] picks a placeholder name for privacy masking.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Selection is for display obfuscation of an already-protected field, not a security token; predictability does not weaken any control.

findings.categoryName: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
findings.title: JSON.parse of a decrypted credential blob
findings.message: const decryptedKey = JSON.parse(...) parses a decrypted credential before persistence.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try/catch and validate with a Zod schema for defense in depth.
findings.demotionReason: Input is server-side decrypted credential data (not raw client JSON), and the result is constrained to Prisma.InputJsonValue; downstream schema typing bounds the shape.

findings.categoryName: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
findings.title: Generic JSON.parse helper returns untyped data
findings.message: return JSON.parse(str) yields `any`, which can flow into typed sinks as a confused type.
findings.recommendation: Return `unknown` instead of implicit `any` and force callers to validate.
findings.demotionReason: This is a shared helper whose callers validate/parse results with Zod schemas before use; the helper itself performs no privileged action.

findings.categoryName: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
findings.sinkText: return await caller.publish(req.query as any /* Let tRPC handle this */);
findings.title: req.query cast to any before tRPC call
findings.message: return await caller.publish(req.query as any) bypasses static typing on the request query.
findings.recommendation: Replace the `as any` cast by parsing req.query with the procedure's input schema.
findings.demotionReason: The tRPC procedure performs its own input validation (Zod) on publish(), so the untyped value is re-validated server-side before any state change.

findings.categoryName: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type (Type Confusion)
findings.title: Error message double-cast to an enum type
findings.message: if (Object.values(ErrorCode).includes(error.message as unknown as ErrorCode)) coerces a string to an enum for comparison.
findings.recommendation: Compare as a string against the enum's string values to avoid the unsafe cast.
findings.demotionReason: The cast is immediately guarded by an Object.values(...).includes() membership test, so an unexpected value simply fails the check rather than reaching a privileged path.

findings.title: API-key delete handler exported via defaultResponder
findings.message: export default defaultResponder(deleteHandler) exposes the [id] delete route.
findings.recommendation: Keep authorization in the route middleware; add a test asserting non-owners receive 403.
findings.demotionReason: Authorization for the /[id] route is enforced by the colocated _auth-middleware.ts (ownership/admin scoping) in the same route folder; defaultResponder is only the response/error wrapper, not the authorization boundary.

findings.title: API-key list handler exported via defaultResponder
findings.message: export default defaultResponder(getHandler) exposes the api-keys list endpoint.
findings.recommendation: No action required; retain the admin gate on cross-user queries.
findings.demotionReason: getHandler scopes results to the authenticated userId (admins may pass query.userId only when isSystemWideAdmin is true at api-keys/_get.ts:20), so records are not returned without an ownership/admin check.

findings.title: Attendee delete handler exported via defaultResponder
findings.message: export default defaultResponder(deleteHandler) exposes the attendee [id] delete route.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: The colocated attendees/[id]/_auth-middleware.ts:15 constrains lookups to `{ id: query.id, booking: { userId } }`, enforcing that only the owning user can act on the attendee.

findings.title: API-key [id] method router dispatches without inline authz
findings.message: defaultResponder(async (req,res) => { return defaultHandler({...}) }) routes by HTTP method.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Each per-method handler (_get/_patch/_delete) is guarded by the route's _auth-middleware and handler-level ownership checks; the dispatcher itself performs no privileged data access.

findings.title: Embed posts messages to the parent with wildcard targetOrigin
findings.message: parent.postMessage({ originator:'CAL', ...data }, '*') broadcasts SDK lifecycle events to any parent document hosting the iframe.
findings.recommendation: Pin targetOrigin to the configured embed parent origin instead of '*' to prevent passive disclosure to unexpected ancestors.
findings.demotionReason: The embed is intentionally hosted by third-party parent pages, and the payload carries only non-sensitive lifecycle/UI events (dimensions, route, link clicks) with no credentials or PII; the inbound side validates message origin/shape.

findings.title: Custom routing page message rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.message: dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: markdownToSafeHTMLClient(customPageMessage) }} injects user-authored markdown.
findings.recommendation: Keep using the sanitizer; periodically review its allowlist against new bypasses.
findings.demotionReason: The content is sanitized by markdownToSafeHTMLClient (an allowlist HTML sanitizer) before injection, neutralizing script/event-handler payloads.

findings.title: Team member bio rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.message: dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: markdownToSafeHTML(member.bio) }} renders profile markdown.
findings.recommendation: No action required while the sanitizer remains in the path.
findings.demotionReason: member.bio passes through markdownToSafeHTML server-side sanitization before rendering, stripping active content.

findings.title: App description rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.message: <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: markdownToSafeHTML(source.content) }} /> renders app-store description markdown.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: source.content is sanitized via markdownToSafeHTML prior to injection.

findings.title: Inline script sets a page-status global
findings.message: dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: `window.CalComPageStatus = '${pageStatus}'` }} writes a status flag.
findings.recommendation: Optionally JSON.stringify the value to harden against future non-constant inputs.
findings.demotionReason: pageStatus is a server-controlled enum/string constant (e.g. '200','404'), not user input, so no attacker-controlled data reaches the inline script.

findings.title: dayjs format string built from a browser-derived token
findings.message: dayjs(...).format(`${detectBrowserTimeFormat}, dddd DD MMMM YYYY`) embeds a locale time-format token in the format string.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: JavaScript has no C-style format-string semantics; dayjs.format only interprets date tokens, and detectBrowserTimeFormat is a constrained 12h/24h indicator, not attacker-controlled conversion specifiers.

findings.title: Composed dayjs format string for insights ranges
findings.message: return `${start.format(`${startFormat} , YYYY`)} - ${end.format(`${endFormat}, YYYY`)}` builds a date-range label.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: startFormat/endFormat are internally derived dayjs tokens; there is no externally controlled format specifier and no printf-style evaluation.

findings.categoryName: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges / Property Injection
findings.title: Request body spread into the booking creation payload
findings.message: { ...req.body } is spread into the object passed to booking creation, a mass-assignment surface where unexpected keys could ride along.
findings.recommendation: Construct the payload from explicitly named, schema-validated fields rather than spreading the raw body.
findings.demotionReason: The booking create path validates/whitelists fields via its Zod schema before persistence, and object spread copies own enumerable keys without invoking the prototype setter, so prototype pollution is not introduced here.

findings.categoryName: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges / Property Injection
findings.title: Request query spread into the cancel handler arguments
findings.message: { ...req.query, allRemainingBookings: req.query.allRemainingBookings === 'true' } merges raw query parameters.
findings.recommendation: Whitelist the specific query fields consumed by the handler.
findings.demotionReason: Query parameters are subsequently validated by the cancel-booking schema, and spread does not set the object prototype; only known, validated keys influence behavior.

findings.categoryName: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges / Property Injection
findings.title: Object.assign augments a request clone with server-derived fields
findings.message: Object.assign(clone, { userId, userUuid, ...oAuthParams, platformBookingLocation }) attaches auth/platform context.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: The assigned keys are server-computed (authenticated userId/uuid, validated oAuth params), not arbitrary user-named properties, so no untrusted key reaches the target object.

findings.categoryName: Execution with Unnecessary Privileges / Property Injection
findings.title: Object.assign adds a computed boolean to an output booking
findings.message: return Object.assign(outputBooking, { isPlatformManagedUserBooking }) sets a derived flag on the response DTO.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: The assigned property is a server-computed boolean with a fixed key; there is no user-controlled property name or value injection.

findings.title: Secrets-generation script writes to a fixed output path
findings.message: fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, content) writes generated env content during setup.
findings.recommendation: No action required for build tooling.
findings.demotionReason: Executed only as a developer/CI script with a build-time constant outputPath; it is not reachable from any runtime request handler.

findings.title: Swagger generator writes the docs artifact
findings.message: fs.writeFileSync(docsOutputFile, stringifiedContents, { encoding:'utf8' }) emits the OpenAPI document at build time.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Runs in the build pipeline with a constant docs output path and no untrusted input; not part of the request surface.

findings.title: App-store CLI writes generated config files
findings.message: fs.writeFileSync(`${appDirPath}/config.json`, JSON.stringify(config, null, 2)) scaffolds an app.
findings.recommendation: No action required for developer tooling.
findings.demotionReason: appDirPath is derived from CLI arguments run by a developer locally; the tool never executes inside the deployed application and processes no end-user input.

findings.title: Slot reservation cookie set without explicit security attributes
findings.message: res.cookie('uid', uid) sets a reservation identifier cookie without explicit HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite flags at the call site.
findings.recommendation: Set explicit { httpOnly:true, secure:true, sameSite:'lax' } attributes for the reservation cookie.
findings.demotionReason: The cookie stores a short-lived, non-sensitive slot-reservation uid (not a session or auth token); compromise does not yield account access, bounding impact.

findings.title: CSRF token cookie issued with an options object
findings.message: res.cookies.set('calcom.csrf_token', token, { ... }) issues the double-submit CSRF token.
findings.recommendation: Verify Secure and SameSite are set in the options for production; HttpOnly may stay off for the double-submit pattern.
findings.demotionReason: This cookie is part of a double-submit CSRF defense and is configured with an explicit options object; it intentionally is readable by the client side of the double-submit pattern and is not a session secret.

findings.title: Edge middleware clears the session cookie on logout/redirect
findings.message: res.cookies.delete('next-auth.session-token') removes the session cookie.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: This is a cookie deletion (clearance), not an insecure set; the original session cookie's security attributes are defined by NextAuth at issuance, so no insecure attribute is introduced here.

findings.title: API-key listing accepts a user-supplied userId filter
findings.message: const userIds = Array.isArray(query.userId) ? query.userId : [query.userId || userId] uses a client-provided userId.
findings.recommendation: No action required; retain the admin gate.
findings.demotionReason: Cross-user querying is reachable only when isSystemWideAdmin is true (checked at api-keys/_get.ts:20); non-admins are forced to their own authenticated userId, preventing horizontal access.

findings.title: Attendee lookup keyed by user-supplied id
findings.message: where: { id: query.id, booking: { userId } } resolves an attendee by a path id.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: The query is ownership-scoped: the WHERE clause requires booking.userId to equal the authenticated user, so a guessed id belonging to another user returns nothing (IDOR prevented at the data layer).

findings.title: Booking listing honors a user-supplied userId filter
findings.message: if (req.query.userId || filterByAttendeeEmails) { ... } branches on a client-provided userId.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Non-admin callers are constrained to their own userId; only system-wide admins may enumerate other users' bookings, so object access is authorization-scoped.

findings.title: Admin-only branch reads query.userId for cross-user listing
findings.message: if (isSystemWideAdmin && req.query.userId) { ... } gates the cross-user path.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: The user-controlled key is consulted only inside an explicit isSystemWideAdmin guard, so non-privileged callers cannot pivot to other users' resources.

findings.categoryName: Exposure of Sensitive Information / Availability Disclosure
findings.title: Raw provider error message returned in the recordings response
findings.message: .catch((err) => ({ ...recording, download_link: null, error: err.message })) surfaces the upstream error text to the API client.
findings.recommendation: Return a generic error string and log the detailed err.message server-side only.
findings.demotionReason: The error originates from the video provider integration (not internal stack traces) and the route is ownership-checked; still, raw upstream messages can leak integration detail.

findings.categoryName: Exposure of Sensitive Information / Availability Disclosure
findings.title: Rate-limit handler returns the error message to the client
findings.message: return res.status(401).json({ message: error.message }) emits the rate-limiter's error text.
findings.recommendation: Map known rate-limit errors to fixed client messages.
findings.demotionReason: The message is a controlled rate-limit/authorization string (not sensitive internal state), and the response participates in the rate-limiting control itself.

findings.categoryName: Exposure of Sensitive Information / Availability Disclosure
findings.title: Global error capture returns a generic 500 message
findings.message: res.status(500).json({ message: 'Something went wrong' }) is the catch-all error responder.
findings.recommendation: No action required; this is the recommended behavior.
findings.demotionReason: This sink already implements the safe pattern: it returns a generic message and does not expose stack traces or internal details to the client.

findings.categoryName: Exposure of Sensitive Information / Availability Disclosure
findings.sinkText: error: { code: exception.name, message: errorMessage }, // exception.name is usually "TRPCError"
findings.title: tRPC exception filter returns a code/message to the client
findings.message: error: { code: exception.name, message: errorMessage } is serialized into the error response.
findings.recommendation: Ensure production builds strip detailed messages for unexpected (non-tRPC) exceptions.
findings.demotionReason: errorMessage is normalized by the filter (tRPC error codes / sanitized messages) rather than raw internal exceptions, limiting information exposure.

findings.title: Booking read-for-authorization precedes the mutating handler
findings.message: const booking = await prisma.booking.findUnique({ where: { id } }) checks the booking before the handler acts on it (check-then-act).
findings.recommendation: Wrap authorization read and mutation in a single transaction (or conditional update) to make the check-act atomic.
findings.demotionReason: The subsequent write is performed under Prisma with row-level constraints/transactions, and the read is used for authorization rather than a value that changes between check and use; practical race exploitability is low.

findings.title: Schedule existence checked before creating an availability
findings.message: const schedule = await prisma.schedule.findFirst({...}) verifies ownership before the create proceeds.
findings.recommendation: Use a transactional create-with-condition to close the window.
findings.demotionReason: The create is constrained by foreign-key/ownership predicates at write time, so a schedule deleted between check and create fails the write rather than corrupting state.

findings.title: Team read in a non-mutating availability GET
findings.message: const team = await prisma.team.findUnique({...}) reads team data to compute availability.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: This is a read-only endpoint with no subsequent mutation, so there is no time-of-use write that a race could corrupt.

findings.title: Availability read in a non-mutating GET
findings.message: const availability = await prisma.availability.findUnique({...}) fetches a single record.
findings.recommendation: No action required.
findings.demotionReason: Read-only access with ownership scoping and no follow-on write; TOCTOU does not apply to a pure read.

findings.title: Per-route credential method allowlist computed in the auth strategy
findings.message: const oAuthAllowed = noSpecificAuthExpected || allowedMethods.includes('OAUTH_CLIENT') determines which credential types may authenticate a route.
findings.recommendation: No action required; keep route-level allowedMethods explicit (avoid relying on noSpecificAuthExpected defaults).
findings.demotionReason: This line IS the authorization control: it constrains acceptable auth methods per route via the route's allowedMethods metadata, rather than being an unguarded sink.

findings.demotionReason: Scope enforcement is centralized in the strategy and applied per route; access requires the route to explicitly opt into the THIRD_PARTY_ACCESS_TOKEN method, limiting token reach.
